ignōrābĭlis , e, adj. ignoro,
I.unknown (rare but class.): separare, quod levius, facilius, non ignorabile, non fortuitum, non necessarium fuerit, * Cic. Inv. 2, 32, 99: “libri litteris ignorabilibus praenotati,” App. M. 11, p. 268 : “alterum illud ignorabilius obscuriusque est,” Gell. 9, 12, 4 (Plaut. Ps. 2, 1, 18, false reading for ignobilis).— * Adv.: ignōrābĭlĭter , in an unknown manner: “laminae ignorabiliter litteratae,” i. e. covered with unknown characters, App. M. 3, p. 137, 6 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
